correctness.rationale: Conditioning on \(N=n\) gives the \(\operatorname{Dirichlet}(1,\ldots,1)\) gap law and the exact regressions \(2/(n+2)\) and \(n/(n+2)\). The Poisson index-shift identity turns their finite differences into equal-and-opposite covariances, and a beta integral gives \(A(\mu)=2[\mu-2+(\mu+2)e^{-\mu}]/\mu^2\). Positivity is analytic. The checker confirms 1001 conditional identities, 10 direct Poisson-sum comparisons, and 3 high-precision small-intensity checks.

value.rationale: Event count and gap irregularity are canonical complementary point-process diagnostics.
